The tour is suitable for anyone -------(21)------- is interested in theatre, including people with no acting experience. As space backstage is limited, advance booking is -------(22)-------. Please arrive fifteen minutes before your chosen session so that staff have enough time -------(23)------- your ticket. For safety reasons, visitors must keep personal bags -------(24)------- the designated lockers during the tour. Photography is allowed in the main hall, but visitors should ask staff -------(25)------- before taking pictures backstage.

Saving Family Photographs

Old photographs often carry stories that family members want to preserve. Before scanning them, people should remove loose dust with a soft brush, -------(26)------- taking care not to scratch the surface. Once the images have been copied, meaningful file names make it easier to -------(27)------- particular photographs later. A short note explaining who appears in each picture may be just as valuable -------(28)------- the image itself. Digital files should also be backed up in a separate location -------(29)------- a single device fails. By involving older relatives in the process, families can record details that might otherwise -------(30)------- forgotten.

groups.instructions: Read the article and answer the questions.
groups.passage:
Water Refill Stations at a Sports Centre

A sports centre introduced three water refill stations after staff noticed that its rubbish bins were often full of disposable bottles. The centre placed two stations near the changing rooms and one beside the indoor courts. Visitors could continue to buy drinks at the reception desk, but they were encouraged to bring reusable bottles.

During the first month, staff recorded how often each station was used. The machine near the courts proved especially popular, and queues sometimes formed between classes. The manager moved a less frequently used station from a changing-room corridor to the entrance of the courts. Staff also added clear signs explaining where visitors could refill bottles.

After three months, the centre reported a reduction in the number of disposable bottles collected from its bins. The manager decided to keep monitoring water use and maintenance costs before ordering any additional machines. She also invited visitors to report problems through a short online form.

questions.question_text: What prompted the centre to install refill stations?

options.text: The reception desk could no longer meet demand for bottled drinks.
The existing refill point by the courts was frequently crowded.
Visitors often left reusable bottles in the changing rooms.
Its bins frequently contained many disposable bottles.

questions.explanation: Đoạn một nói các thùng rác thường đầy chai dùng một lần, dẫn đến việc lắp trạm lấy nước.
questions.translation: Điều gì khiến trung tâm lắp các trạm lấy nước?

questions.question_text: Where was the station with especially high demand originally located?

options.text: At the entrance to the courts.

questions.explanation: Đoạn hai xác định máy gần các sân trong nhà đặc biệt đông người dùng.
questions.translation: Trạm có nhu cầu đặc biệt cao ban đầu được đặt ở đâu?

questions.question_text: Why did the manager relocate one station?

options.text: To replace the need for the original station by the courts.
To encourage visitors to purchase drinks at reception.
To make the changing-room station easier to maintain.
To provide another refill point near the busy courts.

questions.translation: Vì sao người quản lý chuyển vị trí một trạm?

options.text: Continue checking water consumption and maintenance expenses.

groups.instructions: Read the article and answer the questions.
groups.passage:
A Museum Collection Visitors Can Touch

For many years, a small local museum displayed most of its historical objects behind glass. This protected fragile items, but it also limited how visitors could explore their shapes and textures. A teacher working with students who had limited vision asked the museum whether some objects could be experienced through touch.

The museum began by selecting five objects that illustrated everyday life in the past. A craft worker made durable replicas using materials that reproduced important features of the originals. The replicas included a wooden comb, a ceramic cup and a small weaving tool. Staff placed short audio descriptions next to the objects and invited students to test the display.

Feedback revealed that even a carefully made replica needed a clear explanation. Students wanted to know which parts reflected the original accurately and which parts had been modified for safety or durability. In response, museum staff revised the descriptions and provided a brief explanation of the production process.

The new display was later opened to all visitors. Families reported that handling the replicas encouraged children to ask questions about how the original objects were used. Museum staff continued to protect the historical collection while using the replicas to offer a different form of learning. They also began considering which future exhibitions might benefit from a similar approach.

questions.question_text: What limitation of the original display is mentioned in paragraph 1?

options.text: Visitors could not readily explore objects through touch.
Visitors could handle everyday objects but not fragile ones.
Visitors with limited vision could explore textures but not shapes.
Visitors could touch objects only during teacher-led visits.

questions.explanation: Tủ kính bảo vệ hiện vật nhưng hạn chế khả năng khám phá hình dạng và kết cấu bằng xúc giác.
questions.translation: Đoạn một đề cập hạn chế nào của cách trưng bày ban đầu?

questions.question_text: What was the craft worker asked to make?

options.text: Protective coverings that allowed visitors to touch the original objects.
Objects made from the exact original materials without any safety changes.
Robust copies that retained key features of the historical objects.
Models illustrating how the display cases were constructed.

questions.explanation: Đoạn hai mô tả các bản sao bền tái hiện những đặc điểm quan trọng của hiện vật gốc.
questions.translation: Người thợ thủ công được yêu cầu làm gì?

questions.question_text: What does "the originals" in paragraph 2 refer to?

options.text: The audio descriptions prepared for the students.
The historical objects selected for replication.
The first versions of the replicas.
The everyday materials used for the replicas.

questions.explanation: The originals là các hiện vật lịch sử được chọn để làm bản sao.
questions.translation: Cụm the originals trong đoạn hai chỉ đối tượng nào?

questions.question_text: What did the students' feedback lead the museum to change?

options.text: Which original objects should be removed from their glass cases.
The choice of five objects for the initial display.
The decision to let only students with limited vision use the display.
The information explaining the replicas and how they were produced.

questions.explanation: Đoạn ba nói nhân viên sửa phần mô tả và bổ sung giải thích quy trình tạo bản sao.
questions.translation: Phản hồi của học sinh khiến bảo tàng thay đổi điều gì?

questions.question_text: What can be inferred from the families' reports?

options.text: Children were mainly interested in whether the copies were made from original materials.
The tactile display also supported learning for children beyond the original target group.
The audio descriptions alone were responsible for children asking questions.
The replicas were less useful to families than the glass displays.

questions.explanation: Các gia đình nhận thấy việc chạm bản sao khuyến khích trẻ đặt câu hỏi, cho thấy lợi ích vượt ra ngoài nhóm học sinh ban đầu.
questions.translation: Có thể suy ra điều gì từ phản hồi của các gia đình?

questions.question_text: Which statement best expresses the main message of the article?

options.text: Replicas improve learning chiefly when they exactly reproduce all original materials.
A tactile display is most effective when restricted to students with limited vision.
Protecting fragile items requires keeping both originals and replicas behind glass.

groups.instructions: Read the essay and answer the questions.
groups.passage:
Keeping Community Stories Accessible

When a neighbourhood history group began collecting interviews with long-term residents, its members assumed that the most difficult task would be persuading people to share their memories. Many residents, however, were happy to participate. The harder question was how to keep their stories accessible for future readers without losing the context in which they had been told.

The group's first recordings were stored on a single computer. Volunteers gave them file names based on the date of each interview and wrote brief notes about the speakers. When a volunteer tried to find every account of an old market, she discovered that identifying relevant recordings required listening to large sections of audio. Dates helped organise the files, but they revealed little about the subjects discussed.

The group then introduced a simple catalogue. Each entry included a list of topics, the approximate location of events and a description of the speaker's connection to them. Volunteers were careful to distinguish between information provided by the interviewee and details added later by researchers. If two residents remembered the same event differently, both accounts were retained, together with notes indicating the differences. The group believed that such disagreements could themselves be valuable historical evidence.

Another concern involved long-term storage. The members arranged to keep copies in two separate locations and chose widely supported audio formats. They also set a reminder to check the files periodically. They recognised that storing a digital file today did not guarantee that it would remain readable in twenty years. Equipment, software and file formats could all change.

Finally, the group discussed who should have access to the interviews. Some speakers were comfortable with public access, while others wanted particular sections to be available only to researchers. Rather than applying a single rule, the group recorded each person's choices and attached access instructions to the relevant catalogue entries. Volunteers were required to consult these instructions before sharing material.

The project eventually produced an archive that was easier to search and better prepared for future technological changes. Its members learned that preserving a story requires attention to much more than the recording itself. Information about its content, origin and permitted use can determine whether the story remains both meaningful and responsibly accessible.

questions.question_text: What surprised the history group when it began collecting interviews?

options.text: Keeping the stories accessible with their context proved harder than finding willing participants.
Finding interview topics proved harder than convincing residents to participate.
Residents were willing to be interviewed only if recordings were kept private.
Most interviews were easy to catalogue but hard to record clearly.

questions.explanation: Đoạn một nêu nhiều người sẵn lòng tham gia, nhưng việc duy trì khả năng tiếp cận câu chuyện cùng bối cảnh lại khó hơn.
questions.translation: Điều gì khiến nhóm lịch sử bất ngờ khi bắt đầu thu thập phỏng vấn?

questions.question_text: Why were the initial file names insufficient for the volunteer's search?

options.text: They helped locate events but did not identify the date of each interview.
They indicated the interview date but did not identify the person who recorded it.
They did not indicate which topics each interview covered.
They identified the topics but did not indicate the speakers’ connections to them.

questions.explanation: Đoạn hai cho biết tên dựa trên ngày giúp sắp xếp nhưng ít cho biết chủ đề được nói đến.
questions.translation: Vì sao tên tệp ban đầu không đủ để tình nguyện viên tìm kiếm?

questions.question_text: The word "retained" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to -------.
questions.explanation: Retained nghĩa là được giữ lại, trong bài là giữ cả hai lời kể.
questions.translation: Từ retained trong đoạn ba gần nghĩa nhất với từ nào?

questions.question_text: Why did the group record differences between accounts of the same event?

options.text: It wanted to use later research to establish one definitive account.
It considered differing recollections potentially useful as historical evidence.
It needed to identify which topics should be excluded from the catalogue.
It planned to resolve disagreements before granting researchers access.

questions.explanation: Đoạn ba khẳng định chính những điểm bất đồng có thể là bằng chứng lịch sử có giá trị.
questions.translation: Vì sao nhóm ghi chú sự khác nhau giữa các lời kể về cùng sự kiện?

questions.question_text: Which of the following storage practices is NOT mentioned in paragraph 4?

options.text: Converting the interviews into printed transcripts every year.
Checking the stored files from time to time.

questions.explanation: Đoạn bốn nêu ba biện pháp sao lưu riêng, định dạng phổ biến và kiểm tra định kỳ; không đề cập việc in bản chép lời hằng năm.
questions.translation: Biện pháp lưu trữ nào sau đây KHÔNG được đề cập trong đoạn bốn?

questions.question_text: What does "these instructions" in paragraph 5 refer to?

options.text: The guidelines for distinguishing researchers’ additions from interviews.
The notes describing disagreements between speakers.
The reminders to check the audio files periodically.
The access conditions attached to the relevant catalogue entries.

questions.question_text: Which statement best summarises the entire passage?
